slides.title: The managing partner's favourite [is not a strategy].
slides.lede: Before you rename the firm, decide what the name must stop getting wrong.

slides.title: Write the problem [in plain language]
slides.text: "Clients must stop assuming we only provide local bookkeeping" gives a naming team something to solve. "Make us sound ambitious" gives everyone permission to disagree.

items.title: Descriptive
items.text: Immediate meaning, but can confine you later.

items.title: Suggestive
items.text: Points to an idea, needs interpretation.

items.title: Abstract or invented
items.text: Meaning must be built by everything around it.

items.title: Founder or place
items.text: Check what the person or place implies.

cards.label: Companies House
cards.text: Registers the legal entity. It is not trade mark protection.

cards.label: A domain name
cards.text: Gives you a web address. It does not protect the brand.

slides.title: Renaming is [one of three] routes
slides.note: Rename only when **the name itself creates a material constraint**, not because the website feels dated.

slides.quote: Our current name prevents or complicates...
slides.text: Finish the sentence and add the evidence beneath it. If the space stays empty, start with positioning and messaging, not a rename.

slides.title: Define the job before changing the name.
slides.lede: Name types, selection criteria and legal checks for professional firms. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
